title: The Allow Rule Is Right There
symptom: At 09:41 the shop stopped loading for everyone, and SSH from the office stopped working too. The only change today: a colleague added a network rule 'to block one abusive scanner at 192.0.2.66'. They insist the HTTPS allow rule is untouched, and they're right, it is.

goals.description: The shop on vm-web-01 answers HTTPS from the internet
SSH from the office works again

question.prompt: The allow rule exists. Why is everything blocked?
options: NSG rules are evaluated by priority, lowest number first. The new Deny rule sits at priority 90 with source '*', so it matches every packet before Allow-HTTPS (100) is ever reached
A second NSG on the network interface denies the traffic
The route table sends replies to a firewall

solution_commands: az network watcher test-ip-flow -g rg-web-prod --vm vm-web-01 --direction Inbound --protocol TCP --local {web_private_ip}:443 --remote 203.0.113.50:50000
az network nsg rule list -g rg-web-prod --nsg-name nsg-web
az network nsg rule update -g rg-web-prod --nsg-name nsg-web -n Block-Scanner --source-address-prefixes 192.0.2.66
debrief: In an NSG, the first matching rule by priority wins, and lower numbers go first. The intent was fine: a Deny for one bad IP belongs above the Allow rules. But the rule's source was left at '*' (the portal's default), so priority 90 denied the whole internet, and the perfectly correct Allow-HTTPS at 100 was never evaluated. IP flow verify is the fastest way to see this: it names the rule that decided a specific packet, instead of leaving you to read rules and guess. Narrowing the source to the scanner's IP keeps the block and restores everything else; deleting the rule would also work but loses the protection. Manage NSGs as code (Terraform or Bicep), so 'source: *' on a Deny rule shows up in review, and test a firewall change both ways: allowed traffic still passes, blocked traffic is still blocked.
